extracted.intended_audience: authors and writers preparing manuscripts for submission to publishers or editors (including academic authors considering preprints)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how to prepare and format a manuscript for submission and preprint handling across publishing contexts (literary and academic). Covers publisher requirements, the role of style guides, and steps toward final print and authorship documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow publishers' respective formatting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Many publishers still require authors to submit manuscripts formatted according to their respective guidelines. Writers who intend to submit a manuscript should determine what the relevant writing standards are, and follow them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher-specific guidelines are the most critical resource for authors; formatting varies greatly depending on the type of work and the particular publisher, editor or producer. Always check the target publisher's submission requirements before preparing the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use style guides as key references
rubrics_metrics.description: Style guides are key references since "virtually all professional editors work closely with one of them in editing a manuscript for publication."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult an appropriate style guide (e.g., Chicago, MLA, APA) for consistent grammar, punctuation, citation, and stylistic conventions; use them especially where publisher instructions are silent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give precedence to individual publishers' standards over style guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual publishers' standards always take precedence over style guides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a publisher's submission guidelines conflict with a general style guide, follow the publisher. Treat publisher instructions as authoritative for formatting and submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit literary works in standard manuscript format when requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers of literary works such as short stories and poetry often expect submissions in standard manuscript format, which is easily distinguishable from most published material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting fiction or poetry, adopt the conventional 'standard manuscript format' (e.g., plain typewritten layout, specific margins/spacing, title page conventions) unless the publisher specifies otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for a 'final print' with improved layout and proofing
rubrics_metrics.description: A future 'final print' must be planned – with better layout, proofreading, prepress proofing, etc. – that will replace the 'preprinted manuscript'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare manuscripts with the expectation that a separate, more carefully typeset and proofed final version will be produced; include elements (e.g., figure files, high-quality images, clean copy) to facilitate that transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand when a manuscript becomes a publisher's preprint
rubrics_metrics.description: An ordinary manuscript only becomes a 'publisher's preprint' if it somehow gets distributed beyond the authors (or the occasional colleague whom they ask for advice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In peer-review contexts, if a submitted manuscript is not accepted there cannot be a 'publisher's preprint' — 'publisher's preprint' implies distribution beyond the authors under the publisher's auspices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate authorship by depositing versions in repositories or legal deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: In a web context (legal/cultural authorship): to demonstrate authorship, an author can upload a version of their work to a repository before full publication. An alternative could be to use a legal deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institutional or subject repositories, or formal legal deposit mechanisms, to establish a public timestamped record of authorship prior to final publication; check publisher policies on preprint sharing first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare manuscripts using appropriate digital tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Today manuscripts are usually prepared using computers with digital typesetting or word processing software.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use common word processing or typesetting tools (e.g., Word, LaTeX) suitable to your field and the publisher's submission format; provide source files or export formats requested by the publisher.
